models_evaluated: zero-shot general-purpose and specialized foundation models

links.outcome: Zero-shot foundation model AUROC on real EHR-derived hospital operations tasks versus benchmark strength
links.effect: Zero-shot general-purpose and specialized models underperformed on four of five tasks (36.6%-71.7% AUROC); mortality prediction was the exception.
links.quote: In zero-shot settings, both general-purpose and specialized models underperform on four of five tasks (36.6%-71.7% AUROC), with mortality prediction being an exception.

unlisted_practices: In-domain pretraining of LLMs on EHR text
Supervised finetuning of foundation models for hospital operations prediction tasks
Joint multi-task finetuning for cross-task transfer

screen.reason: The paper introduces a specialized EHR-pretrained LLM (Lang1) and a realistic operational benchmark (ReMedE) evaluating tasks like readmission, mortality, and claims denial, testing model performance and transferability without evaluating deployment safeguards or operational practices.
